subject: Physics
subtopic: Vector addition, subtraction, orientation and magnitude-angle decomposition
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

must_contain: Two vectors expressed in one declared axis system with at least one negative component.
The resultant obtained by adding corresponding signed components, with a geometric direction check.

controlled_variation.vary: one input component sign while keeping the other components fixed
controlled_variation.hold: the axis convention and all other component values
controlled_variation.notice: the corresponding resultant component changes by that signed amount

controlled_variation.vary: the order of the two addends
controlled_variation.hold: the same vectors and axis convention
controlled_variation.notice: the resultant is unchanged, exposing commutativity of vector addition

must_contain: A stated target for one resultant component, including a zero-component case.
At least two signed input contributions on the constrained axis so one can compensate the other.

controlled_variation.hold: the zero target on the resultant axis
controlled_variation.notice: the required compensating component changes to the equal opposite signed value

controlled_variation.vary: the target resultant component from zero to a nonzero value
controlled_variation.notice: the required input follows from the same signed component-sum equation rather than a special-case rule

must_contain: A second arrow reversed without rescaling before addition.
The same pair evaluated in both subtraction orders.

controlled_variation.vary: which operand is subtracted from which
controlled_variation.notice: the difference arrow reverses while its magnitude stays the same

ceiling: later-time kinematic evolution after an initial velocity is represented
must_contain: A decision whether the vector needs magnitude-angle decomposition or is already supplied as signed components.
A magnitude-and-angle vector with the reference axis explicitly marked.
An adjacent/opposite decision before sine/cosine is assigned.
A sign check from the declared x/y directions.
Correct binding of the resolved pair to the vector role named by the problem, including u_x/u_y for an initial velocity.
A magnitude/quadrant reconstruction check and an explicit stop before later-time dynamics.

controlled_variation.notice: the adjacent and opposite component magnitudes trade relative size

controlled_variation.vary: the reference axis from +x to +y while describing the same physical vector
controlled_variation.notice: which component uses cosine changes, but the final physical component pair does not

controlled_variation.vary: the quadrant/direction while holding the same acute reference angle and magnitude
controlled_variation.notice: component signs change while the vector magnitude does not

controlled_variation.vary: the vector role from velocity to force or displacement
controlled_variation.notice: the projection rule is generic, while units and contextual component labels follow the vector role

controlled_variation.vary: the input representation from magnitude-angle form to an already-supplied signed component pair
controlled_variation.notice: decomposition is skipped when the component representation already exists

controlled_variation.vary: a velocity context from generic velocity to explicitly initial velocity
controlled_variation.notice: decomposition produces u_x and u_y at the initial instant only; later evolution belongs to Motion-in-2D

family.invariant_demand: Use one declared axis system, preserve signed directional information, combine corresponding vector components, impose any stated resultant-component constraint, preserve subtraction order, and when a vector is given by magnitude plus angle, decide whether decomposition is needed before projecting it into an equivalent signed component representation.
family.difficult_move: Keeping direction and representation roles separate: identify the angle reference before sine/cosine, attach signs from the declared axes, and stop vector decomposition at an equivalent component state rather than smuggling in later dynamics.
family.independent_check: Use an alternate representation: rough arrow geometry must agree with component signs; a constrained component must satisfy its target; swapping subtraction operands must negate the result; resolved components must reconstruct the original vector; an initial component pair must not be treated as a later-time law without a separate motion model.

support_ladder.handed_over: The axis directions, angle reference or component representation, and requested vector operation are supplied.
The axis directions are supplied; the learner must identify whether decomposition is needed and which component is adjacent/opposite.
Only the physical/geometric vector description and requested output are supplied; the learner chooses a consistent representation and stops at the capability boundary.

transfer.changed_demand: Two vectors are described by a diagram or words and must first be written as signed components before they can be added.
A requested direction must be translated into a target value for one resultant component before solving for an unknown input contribution.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which component is constrained and what target value it must take

transfer.changed_demand: The same pair of vectors is presented in the opposite subtraction order.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the final orientation of the difference

transfer.changed_demand: A vector is described verbally or by a diagram, so the learner must identify the reference axis and convert it to signed components without being handed x/y labels.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the explicit angle reference and signed component pair

transfer.changed_demand: A vector is already supplied as signed components, so the learner must decide that magnitude-angle decomposition is unnecessary.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether trigonometric decomposition should be used at all

transfer.changed_demand: The same vector is described using complementary angles from different perpendicular axes and the learner must prove the decompositions are equivalent.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the equality of the two component descriptions
